key_insight: Fusing complementary visual encoders — a contrastive image-text encoder (CLIP-style) and a self-supervised dense visual encoder — produces richer, more robust vision-language representations. The paper shows how to scale this multi-encoder fusion so VLMs gain both alignment/retrieval strengths and dense semantic understanding.
problem_solved: Standard VLMs typically use a single contrastive vision encoder, which is good for alignment and retrieval but misses dense semantics and robustness. The paper addresses how to combine and scale multiple complementary visual encoders so a single VLM benefits from both types of visual knowledge.
method: Dual (or multi-) encoder pipeline: retain a contrastive image-text encoder and a self-supervised/dense visual encoder operating in parallel to capture complementary signals.
Projection & fusion: map each encoder's features into a common representation space and aggregate them via a learnable fusion module so the text encoder can attend to combined visual semantics.

Unified training objectives: jointly optimize cross-modal alignment (contrastive) and complementary alignment or fusion losses to preserve retrieval strengths while injecting dense semantics and robustness.
impact: Provides a practical recipe to build VLMs that keep CLIP-style alignment while gaining richer dense understanding and robustness — improving performance across retrieval, recognition, and downstream multimodal tasks without discarding complementary visual encoders.
